This can also be taken of the resurrection: that he who died for us may be brought to life.
47_marg3269: According to the Septuagint: O Lord, I have heard your word in the Scriptures with the inner ear, and have considered your works, so that from the creatures I might understand the creator, and through them I was astonished; losing the sense of man, I was turned to a holy madness; or, troubled with wonder, I broke out into your praise, saying: In the midst of two living creatures thou shalt be known: that is, through the Son and the Holy Spirit the Father is understood; or the two cherubim, who look toward each other and have the oracle between them; or the two seraphim, of whom one cries to the other the mystery of the Trinity, one of whom, sent, cleanses the lips of the prophet, and says: “I am come to cast fire on the earth; and what will I, but that it be kindled?” But simply: Christ was recognised between two thieves; or by the Jews and the Gentiles, surrounding him on either side; or between the two Testaments, which breathe life.

Or: the earth will be split by rivers, as in an earthquake new springs flow out and others are stopped up; so, the world being shaken by the coming of Christ, the springs of Israel were stopped up and the apostles flowed out. 47_marg3290: As Christ is the head of the Church and of every man, so of all the demons who fight in this world the head is Beelzebub, the prince of the devils; and each of their troops has its heads and princes. For example, the spirits of fornication have their own chief; the spirits of vainglory, the spirits of lying, the spirits of unbelief have commanders of their army. But God, most merciful, where there had been the worst head, often cuts it off and puts in its place the best head. The Hebrews hand down that Reseph is the name of a demon who holds the chief place among the others, and who, for his great swiftness and his running in every direction, is called a bird and a flying thing; and that he it was who spoke to the woman in paradise under the figure of the serpent, and from the curse by which he was condemned by God received the name Reseph, which means “creeping on the belly.”

According to the history, he says in the person of the people that he gladly suffers anything in the captivity, so that he may rest at the time when he curses the sceptres of the wicked and the horses tread the mud, so that afterwards he may return with the saints Zorobabel and Jesus to the land of promise; but the letter of the book does not mean this.

47_marg3302: The fig tree. So I want to suffer here, and afterwards go up to the people that are girded, because the day of tribulation will come, and, while the rest are set in distress, I shall rejoice in your majesty. Or: when the day of the Jews' overthrow comes, I, while the people perishes, am chosen, and shall join myself to the disciples of Christ, going up into the mountains, because he teaches them on a mountain, the crowds left below. For the fig tree to which he came hungry, that is, the people of the Jews, gives no fruit, and so it is cursed; and it bears no fruit, not for ever and ever, but until the age, that is, until the Gentiles have come in. This is the fig tree for which the husbandman pleads, that is, Gabriel or Michael, to whom the people of the Jews has been entrusted, who prays at the Passion: give them time for penance, and do not cut it down; and if it bear fruit (the fig tree is to be understood as left in suspense)… you will move it to another vineyard, that is, the Church. He came three times: through the law, through the prophets, through himself. After the Passion, penance having been granted for forty-two years, because it bore no fruit, it was overthrown. Those who were converted were moved over to the people of the Gentiles, to which the prophet goes up. The vine, that is, the people, which bore no fruit but thorns; not judgement but a cry, saying: “Crucify him, crucify him,” and “We have no king but Caesar”; which after the servants killed the son; and so “the boar out of the wood hath laid it waste.” The olive, that is, the people, whose branches were broken and the wild olive grafted in. Or: the fig tree is the Holy Spirit, for the sweetness of its fruit; the vine Christ, who says: “I am the true vine”; the olive the Father, from whom is all light. In the book of Judges the trees of the forests are said to have come to these trees, that they might reign over them, which never happens; but the bramble rules them, which has thorns and fire, to wound and burn up the fields. Jerusalem, once on the holy mountains, is now called a plain, which feeds not only no rational beings, but not even the cattle and oxen that would carry the yoke of God. All these things will be taken away from the people, because it acted wickedly against God. But if you take the day of tribulation of the end, you will refer it all to those who say they are of the Church but have no works; and the fig tree, the vine, the olive, that is, the Trinity, will not give them its fruit; and not only have they no grain for men, but not even food for cattle and beasts; and instead of the mountains they dwell in the low place.
